title: Geometric Programs for Solenoidal Forcing
main_claim: Thm 1.1: from a machine and input, an effective smooth solenoidal mean-zero force, 1-periodic from time zero, on T^3 with pressure-zero unique solution, such that the particle at (1/4,1/2,1/4) enters {1/2<x<7/8} iff the machine halts. Thm 1.2: arbitrary positive diagonal rectangle maps (source and target lists each separated) realized as period maps on a coding sheet by incompressible shears with normal compensation.

issues.location: body.tex, Sec 3.1, second exact specialization (frontier at one, B=2m+2)
issues.description: The nonhalt bound x<=1/4+2N*l+3l/2 leaves out the l/2 offset from the mode-square origin to its center, so the correct bound is 1/4+2(N+1)l = 9/32. The halt endpoint interval [5/8,5/8+2N*l] should likewise be [5/8,5/8+(2N+1)l]. Both corrected bounds still give <1/2 and lie inside (1/2,3/4), so the conclusion is unaffected.
issues.evidence: The 3l/2 bound is on offsets from the source center, and the center is origin+l/2. With l=1/(64(N+1)), the corrected value is 1/4+1/32<1/2.

coverage:
Theorem 1.1 checked in full:
- Lemma 2.1 (direct forcing) and its energy-uniqueness argument.
- The old-head recorder table: step count 2(J_n-h_n)+3; h_n<J_n with c_0=1 or 2; the inverse test (incoming displacements 1,1,-1,d; written letter determines the predecessor); halting correspondence; idle-start handling of an initially halted machine.
- Lemma 3.1 and the single-cell rectangle formulas: linear part diag(B^-d,B^d); within-family gaps l/B^2 compared with selector collars l/(10B^2).
- Input-shifted chart: initial square separated from the others; nonhalt x stays below 1/2 through shear, translation and lift phases; halt endpoints in [5/8,21/32].
- Selector and height corrections by 1/4 shifts in y and z avoid every tracked path, private height and the coding height. Mean-zero conditions hold. The seven fields W1..W7 produce the stated path.
- Products of shear lists a, b and c verified with sympy. The 3l/2 endpoint bound for list a re-derived by hand.
- Reserved-loader variant (eight axial phases, one Cartesian component at a time): no rule enters M_{q0,0}, loader margins l/(B-1), Xi_c plateau with D=1/16.
Theorem 1.2 checked: the storage/evacuation schedule (13N pulses), the triple (r,zeta)->(lambda r+(lambda-1)zeta, zeta/lambda) with determinant 1, supports missing resting sheets and correction rows, and plateau ranges.
Not audited: Sections 4-6 alternatives (tagged initializer, guarded recorders, remote center, clocks, whole-box parking), the fifteen-phase construction, the material-label section, and the universal-interpreter appendix.
sibling_notes: Family 376 siblings (ranks 328, 494, 475, 496, 518, 453) all no_gap_found. This paper uses the same transverse-pulse/recorder template. It cites companion 'Finite Instructions and Solenoidal Shear Flows' (Thm 3.2, Lemma 2.1) but re-proves the inverse for its own recorder, so no circular dependence was found for Thm 1.1.
